title: A heat proxy reduces resampled ALOHA mixture fits from 79 to 9 percent at fixed local respiration ratios
abstract: We test whether mixtures of earlier Station ALOHA water types plus respiration can match the 2009-2024 oxygen, nitrate, phosphate and salinity means on density 26.4-26.6. Earlier mean profiles fail the point test. Earlier annual values pass with the independently published local O2:N:P ratio 170:13:1, but fail with 138:16:1. A saved fit has a largest weight 1.54 times an equal weight. An added conservative-temperature proxy is at least 0.0282 C too cold for every chemically compatible mixture, even with the full earlier density range. In 500 year-block draws, four-property fits occur in 79.4 percent and joint heat-proxy fits in 9.2 percent. The conditional temperature-gap interval is -0.0186 to +0.1275 C and includes zero. Thus chemical admission alone is insufficient, but the heat test does not give a clear 95 percent rejection. Annual means, approximate heat conversion, fixed release ratios and calibration errors limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, chemical weights and a numerical bound certificate are supplied.
